<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b516e09457f28866230bbd88f72524865fb4aa77` — the merge of head `e4d44dc17119ade5467e3bc47a4db29664e185e5` into base `2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b516e09457f28866230bbd88f72524865fb4aa77 && git checkout b516e09457f28866230bbd88f72524865fb4aa77
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44 e4d44dc17119ade5467e3bc47a4db29664e185e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44 && git merge --no-ff e4d44dc17119ade5467e3bc47a4db29664e185e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2d52e297d33cbbe6e4a3faced827ca66b0eaab44` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0717dd9c5007407bd1b601c06e70c6809b1454dd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/decision-attachments-uploaded-by-caller.integration.test.ts + packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/referenceable-file.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-action.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx

### ① Derived judgments

The face is the narrowing: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on the PR body and the changeset. The two paths before the `+` are the whole floor; every file after it is outside the diff, read and not reviewed. The changeset and `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Gate verdicts, read off this head's check-runs: all 53 runs are completed, 38 `success` and 15 `skipped`, none red. Among the successes: Test Core and its shards 1/8 to 8/8 (the package's vitest `include` is `src/**/*.test.ts`, so the new file runs there), Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure and every Type Check run. Skipped, so not judged here: Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), the UI build, lint and type-check jobs, the opt-in upgrade and tarball jobs. Pending: none.

- **`attachments` on approve, reject and comment, for a non-system caller where `sys_file` is registered: narrowed. Named right.** Absent, `null` or an empty list is not judged. Anything else must be non-empty strings, each exactly the id of a `sys_file` row the lookup reaches under the request's `organization_id` and whose `owner_id` equals `context.userId`. The changeset calls it BREAKING and gives the fix (upload as the deciding user, then attach that upload).
- **A string that is not a `sys_file` id** (the URL-shaped form `normalizeActionAttachment` still reads): refused at these doors. **Named right**, as "an id that names no file".
- **A falsy non-list value** (`""`, `0`, `false`), which used to be stored as no attachments: refused. **Named right**, inside "a value that is not a list of ids".
- **System caller: unchanged. Named right.** One new `isSystem` read; row 43 and the census row of `system-context.mdx` count it (9 sites, one read in `assertAttachmentsUploadedByCaller`).
- **No `sys_file` registered: unchanged. Named right.** `approval-service.test.ts` already drives a user-context comment with attachments over an engine double that exposes no `sys_file`, and stays green.
- **Error surface: no new code.** `VALIDATION_FAILED` is already a row of `handleApprovalError` (400) on the three routes.
- **Published schema: untouched, so no schema face.** `ApprovalDecisionInput.attachments` stays `string[]`; its jsdoc does not state the rule (N5).
- **One guide the diff implies and does not move.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` teaches `attachments: string[]` of `sys_file` ids on approve, reject and comment, without the rule (N5; the lane seat's face).

### ② Semver level

Right. `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` at `patch` is the level AGENTS.md's Post-Task step 3 gives a breaking change that is not a metadata-protocol change. The changeset body carries the BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and exactly one ADR-0087 marker; the PR body carries both declaration lines. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: `attachments` is a runtime input of the decision and comment doors, nothing a metadata author writes. `Clause-②: no` holds: no path under `packages/spec/src/**` is in the diff. Only `plugin-approvals` source moves, so one package is the whole changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question: should the rule widen to "any file the download door serves the caller"? Answered: not in this PR.** The uploader rule is a strict subset of the door's verdict (the door's first arm is the uploader), the in-repo client uploads before it attaches, and the rule needs one column of the file store and nothing else. Widening later breaks nobody; narrowing later would.
- **Escalated to the maintainer, not blocking this head: should these two doors converge on the platform's one predicate?** `referenceable-file.ts` says every write that names a `sys_file` id asks one question (`findReferenceableFile`, bound to the download door's verdict) so that no two doors disagree about which files a caller may take. These doors now ask a second, narrower question, written in another package. If the wider set is wanted, the change is to ask that predicate through a contract the approvals service can reach, never to copy its arms here. That is a change of its own, with its own `Clause-②:` line.
- **`Skills-docs: none`: the reason given greps `skills/` only.** The guide named in ① teaches this input. For the lane seat before ACCEPT: `updated here` or `follow-up owed`.
- **No `Fixes` line:** consistent with a no-card order. Nothing to resolve.
- The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note is owed. No dev flag is left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** It takes part of a declared capability away at the consumer: the contract admits a stored file reference, and the doors now admit the caller's own uploads. It says so as BREAKING, with the fix. It lands inside the platform's rule for a write that names a file (`referenceable-file.ts`: a write references only a file its writer may read), because the caller's own upload is always such a file. Holds.

**`approval-service.ts`: holds against the code it cites.**

- "The download door's own first rule": `judgeFileRead` answers `allow` first when `file.owner_id` equals `context.userId`. The rule compares the same two values, so it admits no file the door would refuse that caller.
- `owner_id` is authorship: `readonly` on `sys_file`, stamped from the session by the upload doors, set to the session's user on any other non-system create, and kept by `copyOwnedFile` on a copy.
- The caller is `actingUserId(context)`, the authenticated principal, never `input.actorId`. An override actor is judged like every other caller; only `isSystem` is exempt.
- The lookup context (`SYSTEM_CTX` plus `tenantId`) has the shape of `systemReadContext`, so the organization wall's verdict for the posture in force decides what "of the request's organization" means. No organization comparison is restated. A request that carries no organization is read with the plain system context, and the uploader comparison is then the whole rule.
- The exemption is the one `referencingCallerOf` gives a system write. The request-to-context composition never sets `isSystem`, and the two in-tree system callers of `decide` (the action link, the SLA sweep) pass no attachments.
- Placement: on both doors after admission and before the first write. On `decideNode` it sits before `assertRunResumable`, whose comment ("last of the refusals") stays true.
- The judged set is the written set. Membership is tested in JS against the ids the read returned, so a collation-loose match admits no other spelling. The bare-id wrap is the engine's own (`normalizeMultiValueFields`), and the lifecycle's `idTokensIn` takes only strings already judged.
- These are the only two writers of `sys_approval_action.attachments` in the service, and approve, reject and comment are the only REST routes that forward the field.
- A failed read and a caller with no user both end in the one refusal.

**The integration test: holds against the scenario it is accepted against.** Real engine, `isolated` posture, the real plugin start. Each refused row discriminates: the other-organization row pins the tenant term of the lookup, the mixed row pins `every`, and both doors assert that nothing was written and that there is one answer. The controls prove admission by the stored row.

Findings. No must-fix and no should-fix; six nits.

- **N1 (nit).** The jsdoc, the test header and the changeset say "a value that is not a list of ids" is refused. The code judges a bare id string as a one-element list and admits it when it names the caller's own file. That is coherent with the engine's scalar wrap; the sentence is one case too wide, and no row pins the bare id. Say "neither an id nor a list of ids", or refuse a non-array.
- **N2 (nit).** `this.engine.getSchema?.('sys_file')`: an engine with no `getSchema` reads as "no file store". `IObjectQLEngine.getSchema` is a required member, so only a test double takes that arm. The jsdoc names the unregistered object alone.
- **N3 (nit).** The one message says to upload again. For a file of another organization that changes nothing, and an administrator overriding a request outside their active organization gets the same answer for their own upload. One answer is the stated design: accepted deviation.
- **N4 (nit).** `status` is not read, so the generic sentence "a write references only a file whose upload was completed" is not asked at these doors. Only the caller's own rows are concerned.
- **N5 (nit, prose face).** The guide and the `Skills-docs:` line (①, ③). The contract jsdoc is a follow-up, since moving it adds the schema face.
- **N6 (nit).** Test gaps that do not weaken the pins: no system-caller control on the decision door, no override-actor row, SQLite only.
